item.title: #MDPI publication: "User Preferences for Cartographic Presentation in Tourist Information Search Across Geographic Scales" The research examines the link between the type of tourist information that is searched for and the graphical level of abstraction, as well as geographic scale. Conclusion: a single type of map that could be useful doesn't exist and different map styles are necessary, depending on the situation. I'm glad there is a study to demonstrate that. 🤣 https://www.mdpi.com/2220-9964/15/3/107
Also important is to think accessibility not as a binary state but as a continuous spectrum considering environmental factors as well as the wheelchair user’s capabilities, skills, and confidence.

They observe sidewalks, ramps, curb cuts, stairs, crosswalks, and streets are the key elements, and length, slope, width, and surface are the key properties that influence #wheelchair #mobility in urban settings.

If you're unsure what to map in #OpenStreetMap for #accessibility, this #MDPI article may help you: "Identifying Key Environmental Factors Influencing Wheelchair Navigation" Read it: https://www.mdpi.com/2220-9964/15/2/75

A new paper published on #MDPI titled "#OpenStreetMap as the Data Source for Territorial Innovation Potential Assessment" concludes that "OSM-based assessments provide spatially detailed targeted, flexible, and replicable insights into regional innovation potential compared to traditional methods. However, the limitations of crowdsourced data, such as variability in quality and completeness, are acknowledged." https://www.mdpi.com/2220-9964/14/3/127

Interesting article and picture gallery of what the agricultural patterns as seen from space reveal about the local practices but also the history. https://www.geographyrealm.com/types-of-agricultural-patterns-visible-from-space/ Naturally, this also reflects in the #OpenStreetMap data, when mappers diligently map individual pieces of farmland. https://overpass-turbo.eu/s/20Dt So, does it imply there could be a way to discover interesting patterns through raw data as well? OSM Teams is a tool for creating teams and roles in the #OpenStreetMap ecosystem for management of groups and communities to organize around existing tools like Tasking Manager, OSMCha, or iD, and improves collaboration. - Found or find a team: https://mapping.team/teams - Video demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GSa4IWxZz4g cc: @openstreetmap #OSMTeams Screenshot of OSM Teams

Not clear yet what the concrete benefits are, but it’s worth noting #OpenStreetMap has been registered as a “Digital Public Good” by the Digital Public Goods Alliance (#DPGA), which is a multi-stakeholder United Nations-endorsed initiative. https://blog.openstreetmap.org/2024/02/05/osm-named-as-a-digital-public-good-by-un-affiliated-agency/ #UN #UnitedNations cc: @openstreetmap
